Adam de Osgodby was appointed by Edward II on 12 November 1307 as keeper (CPR 1307-13, p.15). The petition must date to some time between those dates. It is possible that an order to the treasurer and chamberlains to pay arrears owed to the conversi issued on 28 May 1315 relates to this petition (CCR 1313-18, p.183). However, it refers to different sums than contained in the petition, so it is possible that a date of c.1315. is too late.

description: Petitioners: Thomas Jewe and John de Mouthe. Name(s): Jewe; de Mouthe, Thomas; John. Addressees: King. Nature of request: Thomas Jewe and John de Mouthe request that the king issue letters to the Duke of Lancaster and the Chancellor ordering that Stepelton or another neutral person be appointed as sheriff of Shropshire, and that letters appointing Whytton to the post be repealed. They state that Isolde, widow of John de More, has made a false appeal against them and others regarding the death of her husband, and Jewe has been imprisoned for this for over a year. Whytton is part of their party, and has been appointed despite not having sufficient property as demanded by the statute, and was part of a force of 1000 men who have disseised Mouthe of his manors in Shropshire, for which they have not been fined. Nature of endorsement: [None]. Places mentioned: Shropshire; Marshalsea prison, [Surrey]; Shene (Richmond), [Surrey]. People mentioned: Isolde [de More], widow of John de More; John de More; Thomas de Whytton; John de Stepelton (Stapleton); [John of Gaunt], Duke of Lancaster.
